_comment: Ratchet for scripts/check-alert-copy-claims.mjs, mirroring the convention ops/monitoring/schedule-boundary-rule.json declares for audits/monitoring-schedule-baseline.json: a baselined row REPORTS, a NEW violation (or a baselined row moving to a different violating claim) BLOCKS, and the baseline only ever shrinks. OPS-HOST-KERNEL-REBOOT-W3 CH3.
_key_semantics: <artifact>::<cited path>::<reality>. The reality is part of the key on purpose: if a cited path's reality CHANGES (a build-time gate later becomes scheduled, or a scheduled one is retired), the key changes and the row blocks again rather than staying silently baselined against a fact that no longer holds. Same reasoning as check-claudemd-claims.mjs encoding the asserted VALUE in a claim id, not just its subject.
_why_this_list_is_empty: It is empty because the corpus was ENUMERATED and came back clean after the two real defects were fixed — not because nothing was scanned. Measured at authoring on 34 alert-emitting artifacts, 24 with operator-facing text, 31 repo-path citations: zero cadence claims name a non-scheduled path. The gate prints those counts on every run, so an empty list can always be told apart from a broken scan.
_two_violations_that_were_NOT_baselined_: The first live run reported 2 violations and BOTH were defects in the gate, not in the copy. (a) kernel-staleness-canary.sh's freshly-corrected body was flagged because verb attribution used a character window, which could not separate 'asserted continuously by <the scheduled canary>' from the neighbouring sentence naming the build-time gate; attribution is now per SENTENCE. (b) client-claim-freshness.py was flagged because that same window dragged an unrelated 'hourly' onto a bare pointer, and because the reality classifier read only package.json, so check-boot-readiness.mjs — invoked by .github/workflows/deploy.yml — resolved to UNKNOWN; the classifier now delegates to check-canaries-wired.mjs. Baselining either would have ratcheted in the gate's own bugs and permanently blunted it.
